 This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and reserv
 orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal
 Kumar Paliwal pronounced the following:
 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 18.08.2021 passed by Ist Addl. MACT, Barwani in Claim Case No.32/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,33,800/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.52,300/- (i.e 6,000 x12=72,000+10% FP=79,200 x 6/100 (PD)=4,752x11=52,272(rounded off to Rs.52,300) Medical expenses -Rs.2,44,500/-
Special
diet -Rs.6,000/-

Attendant charges -Rs.5,000/-
 Transportation -Rs.6,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.20,000/-
 -----------------

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.6000/- per month which deserves to be enhanced.
As per the evidence adduced by the appellant, he was working as LIC agent and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other conventional heads is also on the lower side, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
Firstly, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the injured calculated by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves modification.
As per the evidence that came on record, he was working as LIC agent.
He suffered 6% permanent disability to his whole body.
Secondly, the compensation awarded under other conventional heads is also on the lower side which deserves enhancement so as to award just and proper amount of compensation.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be and is hereby modified and enhanced as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.56,628/- (i.e. Rs.6500 x12=78000+10% FP=85,800x6/100 (PD)=5148x11(multiplier)) Medical expenses -Rs.2,44,500/-
Other conventional heads

Like special diet/attender/ Transporation/pain &
suffering/ Loss of amenities etc. -Rs.1,75,000/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.4,76,128/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,33,800/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,42,328/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
